comparison: Both strongly support the core claims about CTFFIND5's improvements (C5, C7, C25-C27, C81-C83). Perfect agreement on claims C74-C75 regarding application to overview images. Both support the practical utility demonstrated in Figure 6, with OpenEval noting visual improvements and appropriate citations, while peer reviewers accept this as a supporting finding without challenge.

Perfect agreement on runtime benchmarking claims C76-C80. Both accept the measurements and caveats. OpenEval explicitly validates the benchmarking methodology and future optimization suggestions, while peer reviewers implicitly accept by not raising computational concerns.

Perfect agreement on limitation claims C92-C95. Both support the authors' transparent scoping of applicability. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of limitations with fair comparisons, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the precision in defining the range of application.

Strong agreement on thickness estimation claims (C48-C50, C52, C54, C56-C57, C86). Both support the novel contribution and improvements. Strong agreement on tomography validation claims C69-C73. Both accept the validation approach and acknowledge systematic discrepancies without challenging conclusions. OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the estimates remain useful despite unexplained systematic differences.

Strong agreement on tilt series validation claims C39-C43. Both support accurate tilt estimation. OpenEval emphasizes internal consistency and agreement with SerialEM calibration, while peer reviewers confirm accurate tilt estimation in general without challenging specific measurements.

Both support aquaporin crystal validation (C34-C35, C103-C104), though OpenEval covers broader claim set (C8-C10, C36-C38). Both emphasize quantitative validation and improved fit resolution. Peer reviewers note compelling evidence for tilted samples specifically.

Partial overlap on tilt series accuracy (C44-C47). Both support the quantitative measurements. OpenEval (R6) covers broader tilt series claims including pre-tilt observations, while peer reviewers focus on overall accuracy demonstration across validation approaches.

Both address scope limitations for single-particle cryoEM (C96-C97). OpenEval covers additional claims about per-particle refinement needs (C98-C99), while peer reviewers emphasize the limited practical application in standard cryoET protocols and praise transparent conclusions.

Partial overlap on scope and application claims (C87-C88). Both support the defined applicability. OpenEval emphasizes workflow optimization benefits, while peer reviewers focus on limitations in cryoET applications and acknowledge precise conclusions about application range.
